name: Abitub
overview: Abitub is a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Shaharaim by Hushim. His mention is brief and focused on his genealogical placement within the tribe, with no additional notes or narratives provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Abitub means '[my] father is good,' reflecting a positive affirmation of paternal character. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Abitub as the son of Shaharaim and Hushim, establishing his direct lineage within the Benjaminite tribe. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Abitub's significance lies primarily in his genealogical role within the tribe of Benjamin, contributing to the biblical record of Israel's tribal ancestry. His mention in 1 Chronicles 8:11 situates him within the broader historical framework of Israel's families, underscoring the importance of lineage in God's providential plan for His people.
